newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SOFTER IN LIQUID MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SOFTER IN LIQUID MARKET.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted largely easier on Monday with liquidity returning to the system after a week-long drought, dealers said.
"The market now has got lots of money. We are expecting Z$461 million (worth of) treasury bills to mature today so we've been forced to bring our rates down," one dealer commented.

He said discount houses were selling treasury bills in the open market at 17.70 percent, down from Friday's 17.85 percent while call money, which peaked at 24 percent on Friday, was on Monday indicated at 18.25 percent.

Bankers acceptance bills were being bought at 18.50 percent from 18.75 and sold at 17.70 percent from their previous 18.50 percent while NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days firmed to 19.50 from 19.25 percent (buying) but softened to 18.25 from 18.75 percent (selling).
Central Reserve Bank figures indicated a pre-settlement surplus of Z$28 million compared to a previous shortage of Z$13 million.
